# Brand vs Performance (Golden Fixture)

Early post-PMF stage: 80% performance / 20% brand.

## Decision cards

### [DEC-080] Brand vs performance split

**Decision:** 80% performance / 20% brand allocation. Brand spend limited to founder content (compounding) + 1 newsletter sponsorship per quarter.

**Why this:**
1. Stage is Early post-PMF; pre-PMF + early post-PMF is 80-100% performance per V3 §1.5.
2. Founder content compounds as brand asset without paid budget.

**Why not the alternatives:**
- 60/40 brand/performance: pre-mature for stage.
- 100% performance: leaves compound founder-content investment on the table.

**Confidence:** High
**Evidence grade:** B (with caveats — Binet/Field methodology critiqued by Sharp).
**Source basis:** Research-backed.

**Commercial-bias flag:** Medium — 60/40 framework heavily promoted by brand-leaning agencies.

**Asset / channel / metric bindings:**
- Performance-attributed: paid-search, newsletter sponsorships, paid-mobile.
- Brand-attributed: founder content (LinkedIn + Hacker News).

**Kill criterion:** If 12 months sustained no aided-awareness lift, reduce brand allocation to 10%.
**Reversal trigger:** ARR crosses $5M with retention solid → shift toward 70/30 brand/performance.
**Test window:** 12 months.

**Anti-pattern to avoid:** Pre-mature 60/40 split at early-stage (per V3 §1.5).

**Cross-cites consumed:** DEC-001 (business model), DEC-067 (readiness), DEC-070 (portfolio).

## What we are intentionally NOT doing
- 60/40 split before $5M ARR.
- Zero brand investment (leaves compound founder content on the table).

## Sources and basis
- V3 Marketing Guide §1.5.
- Binet & Field IPA database (with Sharp critique).
- Evidence grade B.
